title: André Ellefsen to speak at OSJ Americas
summary: Dipai heads to Rio de Janeiro on 13–14 October to share practical applications of maritime expertise, AI and large language models.
paragraphs: Dipai CEO André Listou Ellefsen will speak at OSJ Americas in Rio de Janeiro on 13–14 October 2026. The team will share insights from real-world use cases, focusing on how maritime domain knowledge, AI and large language models are integrated into the platform to create value.

The Americas represents more than 25% of the fleet covered by Dipai’s platform. The region’s energy companies and shipowners are an important part of the company’s work to support digital development in vessel operations.
André will attend alongside Håkon Longva Haram and Edvard Dyb. The team welcomes conversations with customers, partners and vessel operators attending the conference.

images.alt: OSJ Americas 2026 speaker announcement featuring André Listou Ellefsen, with the conference dates and location in Rio de Janeiro.

title: Island Offshore selects Dipai for its entire fleet
summary: A fleet-wide agreement brings the full analytics suite and end-to-end MRV and IMO DCS delivery to Island Offshore.
paragraphs: Island Offshore has selected Dipai to support its entire fleet with the full suite of analytics modules, alongside end-to-end delivery of MRV and IMO DCS.

The collaboration progressed from an initial trial to full-fleet implementation in a couple of months. Dipai welcomed the agreement as a sign of the value the customer was already experiencing and thanked Island Offshore for its trust.
Torbjørn Ingeborgvik, Project Manager Digitalization at Island Offshore, highlighted the speed of implementation, responsive support and the value of the insights already available to the team.

images.alt: Island Clipper offshore vessel alongside an offshore installation.

title: North Sea Shipping chooses Dipai for its subsea fleet
summary: Vessel data collection and Dipai’s full analytics suite will support North Sea Shipping’s advanced subsea vessels.
paragraphs: North Sea Shipping has selected Dipai for its full fleet of advanced subsea vessels. The agreement covers vessel data collection and the complete suite of Dipai analytics modules.
The collaboration brings vessel data and analysis into the company’s work to improve operational performance and efficiency across its fleet.
Sveinung Økland, Operation Manager at North Sea Shipping, welcomed the partnership and highlighted how access to high-quality vessel data and advanced analytics will support better decision-making.

images.alt: Vessel photograph shared with Dipai’s North Sea Shipping partnership announcement.

title: Østensjø Rederi expands its collaboration with Dipai
summary: Following its first vessel onboarding in April, Østensjø Rederi selects the platform for its offshore fleet and selected tugs.
paragraphs: Østensjø Rederi has selected Dipai Digital Fleet Platform for its offshore fleet and selected tugs. The first vessel was onboarded in April 2026, with the collaboration subsequently continuing and expanding.
The platform gives the operator access to operational data for analysing vessel operations, identifying trends and supporting improvements in energy efficiency.

Stian S. Waage, COO at Østensjø Rederi, described the platform as a common source of operational insight that supports the company’s digital transformation and its work to identify further actions under its sustainability plan.

images.alt: Three people on deck beside the Olav Østensjø vessel name.

title: Putting AI to work in offshore vessel operations
summary: Offshore Support Journal features Dipai’s perspective on machinery operation and condition-based maintenance.
paragraphs: Dipai CEO André Listou Ellefsen was featured in an Offshore Support Journal article published by Riviera Maritime Media, discussing how AI can create value for offshore vessel operators.

The perspective shared in Dipai’s post centres on using AI and machine learning to support decisions about engine and genset operation. Where operating conditions allow, running fewer units can reduce equipment wear and support longer maintenance intervals.

The post also highlights anomaly detection in machinery operation as a contribution to condition-based maintenance. Read the original LinkedIn post for the link to the full Offshore Support Journal article.

images.alt: Orange offshore support vessel underway at sea, from the article shared by Dipai.

title: Continuing the decarbonization conversation in Brazil
summary: Dipai returns to the Maritime Decarbonization Alliance Workshop to discuss operational insights with the Brazilian offshore industry.
paragraphs: Dipai attended the Maritime Decarbonization Alliance Workshop in Brazil for the second time. The event was organised by Innovation Norway Brazil and hosted by OSM Thome Brazil.

The team shared its perspective on how operational insights can support maritime decarbonization and more informed decisions. Discussions focused on the challenges and opportunities facing offshore operators in Brazil.
The visit also included meetings with customers and vessel operators. Dipai announced plans to continue those conversations at the Offshore Support Journal conference in Rio in October.

images.alt: Participants at the Maritime Decarbonization Alliance Workshop in Brazil.
Additional photograph from Dipai’s visit to the workshop in Brazil.

title: Håkon Longva Haram joins Dipai
summary: Dipai welcomes a Customer and Product Success Manager with experience across maritime operations and digital development.
paragraphs: Håkon Longva Haram has joined Dipai as Customer and Product Success Manager, bringing experience from both maritime operations and digital solutions.
His career has included roles as Ship Electrician, System Development Engineer and Team Lead for Development. Before joining Dipai, he worked as a Product Manager for digital solutions.
The appointment brings a dedicated focus to customer and product success, strengthening the team’s ability to develop its offering and support customers in getting value from the platform.

images.alt: Håkon Longva Haram, Dipai’s Customer and Product Success Manager.

title: Dipai receives the OSJ Innovation Award
summary: The team celebrates industry recognition at the Offshore Support Journal awards in London.
paragraphs: Dipai received the Innovation Award at the Offshore Support Journal event in London on 3 February 2026, in front of 400 industry professionals.
Almost the full team was together for the evening. The award provided an opportunity to recognise the contributions of the customers and partners involved in Dipai’s development.
In its announcement, Dipai thanked its customers, partners and everyone who voted, as well as Riviera Maritime Media for hosting the conference and exhibition.

images.alt: The Dipai team celebrating the OSJ Innovation Award in London.

title: Dipai at the Annual OSJ Conference in London
summary: The team announced its London exhibition stand and a presentation on turning vessel data into operational results.
paragraphs: Dipai announced its participation in the 2026 Annual Offshore Support Journal Conference and Exhibition in London, with the team exhibiting at stand 13.

André Ellefsen’s session on 3 February focused on how vessel analytics can support practical decisions and measurable improvements. André, Øystein Nordli and Øyvind Wathne Aasmyr were available to meet the offshore community.

title: A year of growth and a new SEEMP module
summary: Dipai’s review of 2025 highlighted a new module, fleet growth and an OSJ award nomination.
paragraphs: During 2025, Dipai introduced its SEEMP module to help customers set operational best practices, attach measurable goals and follow results through vessel data.
The company reported three times as many vessels on the platform and twice as many customers. The update also marked Dipai’s shortlisting for the 2026 OSJ Innovation Award.

title: Joining the Maritime Decarbonization Alliance in Brazil
summary: Dipai joined the alliance’s first seminar and workshop in Rio, alongside shipowners and technology providers.
paragraphs: Dipai travelled to Rio de Janeiro for the first Maritime Decarbonization Alliance seminar and workshop, an initiative of ABRAN. The programme brought Brazilian shipowners together with technology providers to discuss emissions reduction.

The visit also included meetings with customers and other vessel operators. Dipai highlighted Brazil as its largest region for vessels and customers after the North Sea, and noted the interest in using sensor data to support decarbonization.

title: Solstad highlights the value of data in ocean transits
summary: A Riviera feature described how crew experience and Dipai’s dashboards can help Solstad reduce transit fuel use.
paragraphs: Dipai shared a Riviera Maritime Media article on Solstad’s use of connectivity and analytics to improve fuel efficiency.

In the feature, Solstad Sustainability Director Tor Inge Dale described examples of saving 200–500 tonnes of fuel on an ocean transit by combining experienced crews’ knowledge with Dipai dashboards. These were reported examples, rather than a guaranteed saving for every voyage.

title: Dipai completes a €1.1 million investment round
summary: The funding supports further maritime analytics development and customer onboarding.
paragraphs: Dipai announced a completed investment round of €1.1 million.

CEO and co-founder André Ellefsen said the funding would support further development of maritime analytics tools, alongside onboarding new customers and maintaining strong customer support. Dipai thanked the investors and partners supporting the company’s next stage.
